options.label: On the needles
options.description: It could be that one of the stitches isn't sitting the same as the rest of them. It could be a gap between your stitches, or something else!

options.label: In the work
options.description: There could be holes or gaps in your work, or the width has increased or decreaed when you haven't meant for it to. Alternatively, some of the stitches could look different from the rest.

options.label: Unsure
options.description: Look closely at your knitting and the needles, but if you're unsure, that's ok too. We'll try a different way!

q2.title: On Your Needles — What do you see?
q2.subtitle: Examine your working row carefully and match what is active on your needle.

options.label: Extra or missing stitches
options.description: This can be hard to catch! There are either more or fewer stitches than what you started with.
howToTell: Count the number of stitches on your needles, and see if there are more or fewer than the number you cast on with. If the number of stitches has changed, you have either extra or missing stitches.
Your work has gotten either wider or narrower without you intending it to.

options.label: Gaps between stitches
options.description: Extra space between 2 stitches, where the rest are evenly spaced.

options.label: One stitch looks different than the rest
options.description: Maybe you can't quite put your finger on it, but one of the stitches is sitting differently on the needle!
howToTell: Look at each stitch on the needle. Does one naturally slant slightly? If so, this could be your problem.

q3.title: In the work — What does it look like?
q3.subtitle: Closely examine your work below the needles to locate the issue. We call this "reading your knitting"!

options.label: 1 or more holes
options.description: There is a hole or gap in the work.
howToTell: If you stretch and rub the hole, nothing will unravel further.

options.label: A loose ladder
options.description: There is a ladder of looser strands of yarn. at the bottom of that ladder, there are one or more loops that are actively unraveling.
howToTell: 1+ stitches actively unraveling.
If you pull at the loose stitch, it will come undone further, creating another rung in the ladder.

options.label: Stitches look like Y's instead of V's
howToTell: Stretch your work. If the part you suspect is the problem is also significantly less stretchy, there's a good chance you're correct.

options.label: Work has changed size
options.description: The work is getting narrower or wider, in a way you weren't expecting.
howToTell: There are fewer or more stitches on the needles than the number you casted on.

q4.title: No problem. We'll figure it out!
q4.subtitle: Can you see any of these?

options.label: Extra or missing stitches
options.description: This can be hard to catch! There are either more or fewer stitches than what you started with.
howToTell: Count the number of stitches on your needles, and see if there are more or fewer than the number you cast on with. If the number of stitches has changed, you have either extra or missing stitches.
Your work has gotten either wider or narrower without you intending it to.

options.label: A loose ladder
options.description: There is a ladder of looser strands of yarn. at the bottom of that ladder, there are one or more loops that are actively unraveling.
howToTell: 1+ stitches actively unraveling
If you pull at the loose stitch, it will come undone further, creating another rung in the ladder.

options.label: Stitches that look like Y's instead of V's
options.description: Some of the stitches do not look like the others. They are slightly slanted and less stretchy. You could say that they look more like lowercase y's than v's
howToTell: Stretch your work. If the part you suspect is the problem is also significantly less stretchy, there's a good chance you're correct.

q5.title: Do the holes look like either of these?

options.label: A secure hole
options.description: If you stretch and pull the hole, it does not get worse.

options.label: A hole that might be getting bigger
options.description: If you stretch and pull the hole, a loop drops and unravels further.

q6.title: Look closely at the work
q6.subtitle: Can you see one stitch become two anywhere?

options.label: Yes
options.description: This is called an increase, and sometimes we can do it without meaning to. Look at your work and see if there's anywhere where 1 V turns into 2 V's.
howToTell: One column of V stitches becomes two.

options.label: No
options.description: You have checked each column of v's from the bottom to the top of the knitting, and there is no extra column added.

q7.title: Has your work gotten wider or narrower?

options.label: Wider
options.description: This happens from increases. A good way to tell is to count your stitches, and see if there are more than there were when you cast on.
howToTell: There are more stitches than the number you started with.
Your work has grown in size from the cast on edge to the stitches on your needles.

options.label: Narrower
options.description: This happens from decreases. A good way to tell is to count your stitches, and see if there are fewer than there were when you cast on.
howToTell: Fewer stitches on the needles than when you cast on.
2 or more columns of stitches have become 1 column.

q8.title: Do you also see a hole in your work?

q9.title: What looks different?
q9.subtitle: Look closely at the individual stitch, just below the needle. Compare it with these pictures.

options.label: The two legs of one stitch cross at its base instead of forming an open V.
The needle passes through only part of the yarn strand, leaving some fibres outside the loop.

q10.title: What can you see beneath the gap?
q10.subtitle: Keep the stitches on your needles while you look. Match the gap to one of these pictures.

options.label: A loose loop below the needle, with a horizontal strand or ladder of strands above it.
An extra loop over the needle, with an opening beneath it instead of a stitch directly below.
None of these / I'm not sure.

q11.title: How does this stitch look different?
q11.subtitle: Compare the unusual stitch with the stitches beside it.

options.label: Some fibres of the yarn have been caught separately, leaving the rest outside the stitch.
Its two legs cross at the base instead of forming an open V.
It looks like an extra loop over the needle, with no stitch directly beneath it.
None of these / I'm not sure.

q12.title: Can you see where a stitch went missing?
q12.subtitle: Look below the needles and compare your work with these pictures.

options.label: There is a loose loop, possibly with a ladder of horizontal strands above it.
howToTell: If you pull at the loose stitch, it will come undone further, creating another rung in the ladder.
1+ stitches actively unraveling.

sidequest-1.title: How many stitches did you cast on in the beginning?

sidequest-2.title: Now, let's count your stitches.
sidequest-2.subtitle: Count each loop of yarn that is on the needle. How many do you see now?

uncertainResult.title: Let's take another look
uncertainResult.subtitle: We haven't found a clear match yet. You can compare your work with more pictures or change an earlier answer.
